extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry/number theory familiar with Mochizuki's Inter‑Universal Teichmüller (IUT) theory
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and structural requirements for building and manipulating subquotients, log-links, Frobenioids, prime-strips, and related objects in the LGP/LGP‑Gaussian log‑theta‑lattice context of IUT; includes compatibility/incompatibility conditions, definitional conventions for log-volumes, and design tradeoffs between multiplicative and additive models. Targeted at constructing the closed-loop chains of poly‑isomorphisms needed to compute projections (Θ‑intertwining → q‑intertwining).

rubrics_metrics.name: sQ1: Kummer-detachment indeterminacies
rubrics_metrics.description: The (sub)quotient operation labeled (sQ1) — i.e., Kummer-detachment indeterminacies — which moves from objects that contain certain étale-like structures to 'purely' étale-like structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussed in detail in Remarks 1.5.4, 2.1.1, 2.2.1, 2.2.2, 2.3.3 and Remark 3.10.1 (ii),(iii). sQ1 is one of the subquotient operations whose nontriviality arises from balancing introduced indeterminacies with compatibility with pre-quotient structures; used in forming poly-isomorphisms of F (cid:4)(cid:5)×μ-prime-strips.

rubrics_metrics.name: sQ2: Galois evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: The (sub)quotient operation labeled (sQ2), Galois evaluation, i.e., evaluation operations that use Galois theoretic data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referenced to [IUTchII], Remark 1.12.4; appears as horizontal arrows in commutative diagrams (e.g., Remark 3.10.2). Compatibility with Kummer theory and issues arising are discussed in [IUTchII], Remark 1.12.4.

rubrics_metrics.name: sQ3: Passing to hulls and determinant positive tensor powers
rubrics_metrics.description: The operation (sQ3) consisting of passing from more general regions to positive tensor powers of determinants of hulls and then applying the (cid:11)-formalism (set-theoretic/stack-theoretic quotients).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delicate issues include tensor-power-twist indeterminacies (Ob4-3), the (cid:11)-formalism (Ob5), and compatibility with log-Kummer correspondences (Ob7). See (Ob1)–(Ob7) and the discussion in (ix) for stabilization by Ok, formation of det⊗M(φ(PB)), construction of (cid:11)-categories of objects and local-global (cid:11)-collections, and interpretation as formal or stack-theoretic quotients rather than coarse/set-theoretic quotients.

rubrics_metrics.name: sQ4: Adjust vertical shifts via log‑Kummer correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: The operation (sQ4): adjusting vertical shifts in the vertical column of the log-theta-lattice (codomain of the Θ LGP-link) by applying the log‑Kummer correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This adjustment produces an indeterminacy with respect to arbitrary iterates of the log-link (Ob8). It is described as being tautologically compatible with suitable isomorphisms between local Galois groups and units/Frobenius-like units (see (cQ4) and vertical coricity of Theorem 1.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: sQ5: Passing to log‑volumes
rubrics_metrics.description: The operation (sQ5) of passing from objects/regions to their log-volumes via realified semi-simplifications (see Remark 3.9.4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passing to log-volumes introduces subtleties in compatibility with log-links and log‑Kummer correspondences (Ob3, Ob4, Ob6, Ob7, Ob9). Notably, sQ5 forgets local Galois groups and Frobenius-like units (see (iQ5)). Compatibility issues and detailed discussion in Remark 3.9.4 and (vii) of Remark 3.9.5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design balance: minimize indeterminacies while preserving compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A general design criterion: each (sub)quotient operation must strike a delicate balance between minimizing indeterminacies introduced by passage to a quotient and ensuring compatibility with the pre-quotient structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is emphasized as the source of nontriviality of the operations (sQ1)–(sQ5). The text repeatedly highlights that choosing quotients requires careful control of indeterminacies so as not to destroy compatibility needed for later constructions (e.g., forming closed loops of poly-isomorphisms).

rubrics_metrics.name: cQ3: Compatibility of sQ3 with F (cid:3)×μ-prime-strip data
rubrics_metrics.description: Compatibility condition (cQ3): hulls ∈ H stabilized by Ok imply that, after taking suitable positive tensor powers of determinants, one obtains objects in local/global Frobenioids that carry faithful actions of local Galois groups Gv and units O×μ; thus sQ3 is compatible with the F (cid:3)×μ-prime-strip data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By considering pull-back morphisms in local Frobenioids, one obtains objects with faithful Gv and O×μ-actions corresponding to the F (cid:3)×μ-prime-strip portion of F (cid:4)(cid:5)×μ-prime-strips. The quotient induced on H by the (cid:11)-formalism corresponds to a (cid:11)-category of objects equipped with 'structure poly-morphisms' and compatible morphisms; formal/stack-theoretic quotient viewpoint is important (see (ix)).

rubrics_metrics.name: cQ4: Compatibility of sQ4 with F (cid:3)×μ-prime-strip data
rubrics_metrics.description: Compatibility condition (cQ4): the vertical‑shift adjustment in sQ4, obtained via the log‑Kummer correspondence, is tautologically compatible with isomorphisms between local Galois groups Gv and étale‑like units O×μ(Gv) or Frobenius‑like units, up to indeterminacy from iterates of the log‑link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tautological compatibility follows from vertical coricity (Theorem 1.5 (i)). One must allow an indeterminacy relative to arbitrary iterates of the log-link (Ob8).

rubrics_metrics.name: iQ5: Incompatibility of sQ5 with F (cid:3)×μ‑prime‑strip data
rubrics_metrics.description: Incompatibility condition (iQ5): passing to log‑volumes (sQ5) precisely forgets the local Galois groups and Frobenius‑like units — i.e., it is incompatible with retaining the F (cid:3)×μ‑prime‑strip portion of the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This contrasts with sQ3 and sQ4 which preserve arithmetic holomorphic structures; the text frames iQ5 as 'forgetting arithmetic holomorphic structure' or incompatibility with the log‑Kummer correspondence on the vertical column. Consequence: sQ5 cannot substitute for sQ3/sQ4 when one needs to retain local Galois/unit data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closed‑loop requirement for chain of poly‑isomorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: The chain of poly‑isomorphisms (involving sQ1, sQ2, sQ3, sQ4, and then sQ5) must form a closed loop (up to formal quotient indeterminacies) to compute the projection of the Θ‑intertwining onto the q‑intertwining; non‑closure yields no nontrivial conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, the path begins from the q‑pilot F (cid:4)(cid:5)×μ‑prime‑strip in the codomain, passes through the Θ LGP-link and the poly‑isomorphisms induced by sQ1 and sQ2, and finally through sQ3 and sQ4 (which satisfy compatibility). Omitting sQ3 or sQ4 or skipping steps breaks the loop and prevents deriving the intended consequences (see discussion in (viii) and related remarks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Must use multiplicative arithmetic line bundles (avoid additive rank>1 categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not possible to avoid passing to hulls by replacing local/global Frobenioids with more general categories of regions ∈ P; the LGP‑link requires purely multiplicative categories (arithmetic line bundles, rank 1) rather than additive higher‑rank vector bundles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the LGP‑link is not compatible with additive structures in domain and codomain, gluing must be multiplicative. Attempts to norm/determinant down to Q or Qpv fail to extend Galois‑equivariantly due to lack of splitting of decomposition groups (Gpv). Thus arithmetic line bundles over Fmod or Kv (with stack-theoretic twists at Vbad) are the correct objects (cf. discussion around (x), Ob1–Ob4, and Ill‑suited norm operations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Log‑link compatibility implies compatibility of product formulas and global arithmetic degrees
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition 3.9 (iv) log‑link compatibility: coincidence of log‑volumes for sufficiently small regions implies compatibility of 'product formulas' (ratios of conversion between log‑volumes at distinct v ∈ V) and hence compatibility between global arithmetic degrees in domain and codomain of the log‑link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The log‑link compatibility refers to certain sufficiently small regions, and the product formula can be formulated in terms of those. Hence, checking log‑link compatibility suffices to ensure equality/compatibility of product formulas and global degrees (see Remark 3.9.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and handling of log‑volume (single sets and collections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition: the log‑volume of a relatively compact subset E ⊆ I Q((−)) is the infimum of log‑volumes of supersets E* ∈ M(I Q((−))) with E ⊆ E*; similarly for collections {EvQ} one takes infima over supersets or views them as inverse systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow that log‑volume of E or a collection may be −∞; equivalently, treat E as an inverse system of E* with finite log‑volumes to always work with finite values. For direct product pre-regions, use inverse systems of direct product regions to ensure finiteness (see Remark 3.9.7 (ii),(iii)). This is practical guidance for computing/estimating log‑volumes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice between F (cid:3)_MOD (LGP) and F (cid:3)_mod (lgp): multiplicative vs additive tradeoffs
rubrics_metrics.description: A modelling/choice criterion: F (cid:3)_MOD (LGP) is multiplicatively biased, admits precise log‑Kummer correspondences, and is well‑suited to computing Kummer‑detachment indeterminacies; F (cid:3)_mod (lgp) is additively biased, better related to mono‑analytic log‑shells and suited to computing étale‑transport indeterminacies and explicit estimates via log‑volumes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fig. 3.2 summarizes the tradeoffs: MOD/LGP structures are rigid and precisely compatible with log‑Kummer correspondences but ill‑suited to computing étale‑transport indeterminacies; mod/lgp structures are distorted but suited to explicit computation/estimates of global arithmetic degrees via log‑volumes (Proposition 3.9 and Corollary 3.12). Choose the model according to whether one needs precise Kummer compatibility or computability of estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Log‑Kummer correspondences and Frobenioid isomorphisms must be mutually compatible with log‑links
rubrics_metrics.description: Kummer isomorphisms/functorial algorithms (vertical coricity) induce Frobenioid isomorphisms and F (cid:4)⊥‑prime‑strip isomorphisms that must be compatible, as m varies, with the log‑links of the LGP‑Gaussian log‑theta‑lattice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This compatibility is required to avoid Kummer‑detachment indeterminacies and to ensure the induced isomorphisms of F (cid:4)⊥‑prime‑strips behave well under iterates and translations (see Proposition 3.10 (i)–(iii) and Remark 3.10.1). These mutual compatibilities underpin the constructions of evaluation isomorphisms and the commutative diagrams reviewed in Remark 3.10.2.
